cover.headline:
One Notion your team
and your agents trust.
cover.lede: A three-phase plan to organize Biomed's Notion so you, Chris, Elizabeth and your AI agents all work from the same place, with your first two agents built and tested. Based on our conversations on October 29, November 10 and November 13.

glance.p: The structure your agents will read from and write to.
Three phases in about five weeks.
On a new workspace, at no cost.

context.title:
What we
heard.
context.lede: Biomed is a three-person recruitment agency moving to Grok as its central AI. Recruiterflow stays as the ATS, but everything else is spread across Planner, SharePoint, OneDrive, OneNote and a new Notion workspace, and the agents can only be as good as the place they read from.

stats.t: tools for tasks, files and notes: Planner for tasks, SharePoint and OneDrive for files, and a new Notion workspace

pains.p: Ten years of notes, plus SharePoint and OneDrive, with no clear rule for what lives where. Grok can't find what nobody can find.

pains.h: Every new job starts in Planner
pains.p: Assigning tasks to Chris and Elizabeth for each new role is done by hand, and Planner doesn't talk to Grok.
Chris and Elizabeth aren't on Notion yet, so the system only works for one person.

quote.text: I do like how Grok can just pull things without me going into Notion, but I also wanna keep Notion organized and clean, too.

context.opportunity: You're about to build agents for recruiting, metrics and sales. If Notion is organized first, every agent starts with the right context instead of each one needing its own fix later.

focus.title:
Where we'd
start.
focus.statement: One organized Notion that your team and your AI agents work from, and a clear plan for what to automate next. We start with the foundation and the two agents that save you the most time, then teach your team to build the rest.
asked: Organize Notion, with a private space for your personal tasks
Notion as the brain for your agents
Tasks assigned automatically for every new job
Metrics from your Excel and Recruiterflow, ready for 2027
Clean up OneNote, SharePoint and OneDrive
Automate as much of your recruitment process as possible
recommend: Clean architecture, with personal and team spaces
One map of where each metric and file lives across your tools
Your recruitment process broken down: what to automate, what an agent drafts, what stays human
The two agents that save the most time, built and tested with you
Tasks that create themselves for each new job, for the team and for you
Training so your team builds the next agents
focus.why: Your process has many steps. Some are already automated in Recruiterflow and some are conversations that should stay human. Mapping it first means we build the agents that actually save time, instead of automating everything at once.

proposal.title:
What we'll build
and what it costs.
proposal.intro: Each phase has its own price and they add up to one fixed total. Under each phase you'll see what we deliver and what we need from you.

phases.name: Audit, process map and architecture
phases.summary: We review your workspace, your tools and your RF - Full Recruitment Process, then decide where everything lives and what is worth automating.

deliverables.p: What to keep, change or archive in your current workspace and the blueprint you received.
Teamspaces with separate personal and team sections. Your current Notion content moved in, unused pages archived.

Where each metric comes from (Recruiterflow, QuickBooks, Reply.io or Notion) and what stays in each tool. It answers whether your placement data needs a Notion database or can all live in Recruiterflow.

We import the cleaned metrics Excel your team prepares into the place the data sources map recommends: Recruiterflow, with custom fields that keep your original dates, or a placements database in Notion.
Every step of your RF - Full Recruitment Process mapped out, marking what Notion can automate, what an agent can draft for your review, what stays in Recruiterflow and what stays with your team.
The agents and automations worth building, ranked by how often each step happens and how much time it saves.
What moves from OneNote, SharePoint and OneDrive, what stays (linked from Notion), and how to move it, by hand or with AI.

you_do: Migrate your documents with the guide

phases.name: Context layer and your first two agents
phases.summary: The context any AI agent reads from, and your first two agents, built in Claude or Grok and tested in your real work. One of them can be your metrics agent.

deliverables.p: The rules your agents follow, adapted to Biomed: approval before sending, archive instead of delete.
The databases your agents read from, in their own teamspace.
Your Notion and Loom recordings in one place, feeding the agents' memory after every call.
The top two from the Phase 1 priority list, for example a metrics agent and a recruiting agent, built in Claude or Grok and connected to Notion. You choose the final two.
You use both agents in your work for a week, then we meet, collect your feedback and adjust them.
Instructions your team copies to create the next agents from the list.

you_do: Use both agents for a week

callout.title: Your metrics agent

items.q: What's our retention rate for the last three years?
Make a one-pager with our track record for a new client.

callout.note: If you choose it as one of your two agents.

phases.name: Tasks, automations and training
phases.summary: Team and personal tasks in one place, tasks that create themselves for each new job, and a team that knows how to keep automating.

deliverables.p: Your Planner tasks moved into Notion, for the team and for your personal and day-to-day tasks. Your personal tasks stay private.
Each new job creates its tasks by job type, already assigned to Chris and Elizabeth.
A page for each team member with their tasks for the day.
Using the workspace, building Notion automations, and building the next agents from the Phase 1 list.
How the team uses the workspace day to day.

included: One working session with you every week (five in total)
3 months of Notion Business on a new workspace, at no cost
excluded: Agents beyond the two built in Phase 2 (your team builds the next ones after the training, or we scope them separately)
Automations and integrations beyond the ones listed in each phase (subject to technical feasibility)
Ongoing data entry and custom dashboards (keeping the data current happens in Recruiterflow or through your agents)
Moving files from OneNote, SharePoint or OneDrive (the migration guide shows you how)
Notion licenses after the bonus period
proposal.guarantee: Two weeks of async support after the last delivery to fix issues within the delivered scope, at no extra cost.

payment.schedule: 50% when you accept, 50% on delivery. By bank transfer, or by card through Stripe with a 4% card fee.
